name: Red Sea
genZNote: The Red Sea is the narrow hallway between the Indian Ocean and the Mediterranean — block it (or the Suez Canal at its end) and a huge chunk of world trade has to take the long way round Africa.

sections.heading: 🌊 Location & Ocean Connection
bullets: A long, narrow sea between north-eastern Africa and the Arabian Peninsula.
Connects to the Indian Ocean in the south through the Bab-el-Mandeb strait and the Gulf of Aden, and to the Mediterranean Sea in the north through the Suez Canal.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Countries Bordering It
bullets: Egypt, Sudan, Eritrea, Djibouti on the African side; Saudi Arabia, Yemen and Jordan (a short coastline) on the Arabian side; Israel has a small coastline at its northern tip (Gulf of Aqaba).

sections.heading: 🚢 Ports & Trade Routes
bullets: Major ports: Jeddah (Saudi Arabia), Port Sudan, Suez and Safaga (Egypt), Djibouti (also a major regional hub near Bab-el-Mandeb).
The Red Sea-Suez Canal corridor is the primary shortcut between Europe/the Mediterranean and Asia — the alternative is the much longer route around Africa's Cape of Good Hope.
Carries a major share of global container and energy shipping between Europe and Asia.

sections.heading: 🐠 Economic & Ecological Significance
bullets: Known for exceptionally warm, salty water and some of the world's most well-preserved coral reefs, particularly off Egypt's Sinai coast and Sudan.
High salinity is due to high evaporation rates and limited freshwater inflow (no major rivers empty into it).
A globally significant recreational diving and marine-tourism destination because of its reef biodiversity and clear water.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Red Sea is a narrow sea between north-east Africa and the Arabian Peninsula, linking the Indian Ocean (via Bab-el-Mandeb) to the Mediterranean (via the Suez Canal).
keyFacts: Links Indian Ocean to Mediterranean via Bab-el-Mandeb and the Suez Canal.
Borders Egypt, Sudan, Eritrea, Djibouti, Saudi Arabia, Yemen.
Very high salinity; no major rivers flow into it.
commonConfusion: The Red Sea and the Suez Canal are different things — the Red Sea is a natural sea, the Suez Canal is a man-made waterway at its northern end.

highYieldFacts: Red Sea connects Indian Ocean (via Bab-el-Mandeb) to Mediterranean (via Suez Canal).
Very high salinity — high evaporation, no major river inflow.
commonTraps: Don't say the Red Sea 'is' the Suez Canal — the canal is a separate, connected structure.
mustRemember: Red Sea = Europe-Asia shipping shortcut via Suez; extremely saline; major reef ecosystem.
